annex

/uh-NEKS/ - rhymes with checks · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Annex means to take control of territory or space and make it part of one's own.

When the bakery outgrew its kitchen, the owners annexed the vacant barbershop next door and knocked through the wall within a month.

Example

The hospital quietly annexed the parking structure across the street: new signs went up, the entrance was rebuilt to face the wards, and the deed now lists it as part of the medical campus.

Annex is more precise than 'take over' or 'use' because it means formally making a space part of your own — not just holding it or borrowing it, but redrawing the boundary so it belongs to you.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

absorb: To absorb is to take something in until it vanishes into the whole — no deed, no boundary, no formal claim. Annex is narrower: it applies to territory and space, formally redrawn to become yours. A firm can absorb a rival's staff; it annexes the office floor.

incorporate: To incorporate is to fold something into a larger body, often on paper and by agreement — a merger both sides sign. Annexing is one-sided: the annexed space is simply claimed, agreement or not, and the boundary is redrawn by the taker.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

cede: to give territory or control away — the exact reverse of taking it

return: to hand something back to the owner it came from

Where it sits · how fully ownership changes hands — borrow → occupy → annex

borrow vs. annex: Borrowing the empty lot is far milder than annexing it — you use it for a season and hand it back, and nothing about who owns it ever changes.

occupy vs. annex: Occupying a space is weaker than annexing it — you hold it and use it, but it never becomes yours on paper.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — an-

Prefix — an-: to, toward (a form of Latin ad-)

Root — nex

Root — nex: to bind, to tie (Latin nectere, nexus)

Put it together

Put it together: An- (a form of ad-, 'to') + nex (to bind, tie) = to tie something onto what you already hold. When a city annexes the land beside it, the new ground is literally bound to the old — one boundary line, one owner, one map.

Use the root in a new word: connect

Use the root in a new word: connect: By senior year, the debate room had become the nexus of campus politics.

Word Choice

formal / official

Annex is the formal word for making territory or space part of your own — governments annex provinces, campuses annex buildings. For casual grabbing, 'take over' works; reach for annex when the boundary itself is being redrawn. Its unit-mate subjugate takes a people, not a place: you annex land, but you subjugate the people living on it.
